tasks.goal: Build a Python standard-library line-oriented JSON service in main.py backed by SQLite at /tmp/stock_reservation_ledger.db. Read one UTF-8 JSON value per stdin line; emit exactly one JSON object per line and no stdout logs. State persists during process; a fresh process is empty. Parse each line independently: malformed JSON returns exactly {ok:false,error:'invalid_request'} and processing continues with the next line. For each valid JSON value, require an object with exactly operation-specific keys: stock={op,sku,quantity}, reserve={op,request_id,sku,quantity}, release={op,request_id,reservation_id}, list={op}; missing or extra keys are invalid_item. SKU and IDs are nonempty case-sensitive strings. Quantities are JSON integers, never booleans, in [0,9223372036854775807], with reserve quantity positive. Validate request shape and field types before checking idempotency. stock {op:'stock',sku,quantity} sets total physical stock while preserving active reservations; if total would be below reserved quantity, return {ok:false,error:'insufficient_stock'} without mutation. Success is {ok:true,sku,quantity}. reserve {op:'reserve',request_id,sku,quantity} atomically succeeds only when SKU exists and available stock suffices; an unknown SKU or insufficient stock returns {ok:false,error:'insufficient_stock'} without mutation. Success is {ok:true,request_id,sku,quantity}, and reservation_id equals request_id. request_id is globally unique across reserve/release: after shape/type validation, an exact operation+field replay returns the originally stored response without additional mutation, even if stock/reservation state has since changed; any differing operation or field under the ID returns {ok:false,error:'idempotency_conflict'} before mutable stock or reservation-state checks. Failed requests do not consume IDs. release {op:'release',request_id,reservation_id} releases an active reservation; success is {ok:true,request_id,reservation_id,released:true}. For a new request ID, an unknown reservation returns {ok:false,error:'reservation_not_found'}; an already released reservation returns {ok:false,error:'reservation_already_released'}. Failures do not mutate or consume IDs. list {op:'list'} returns {ok:true,items:[{sku,quantity,reserved,available}]} for every ever-stocked SKU, sorted by SQLite binary lexical order; reserved is active reservation sum and available=quantity-reserved. Any valid JSON non-object input, invalid field/value, or unknown operation returns exactly {ok:false,error:'invalid_item'}. All failures preserve state.

Build a Python standard-library line-oriented JSON service in main.py backed by SQLite at /tmp/wallet_transfer_ledger.db. Read one UTF-8 JSON value per stdin line; emit exactly one JSON object per line and no stdout logs. State persists during process; a fresh process is empty. Parse each line independently: malformed JSON returns exactly {ok:false,error:'invalid_request'} and processing continues with the next line. For each valid JSON value, require an object with exactly operation-specific keys: deposit={op,account,amount}, transfer={op,transfer_id,from,to,amount}, list={op}; missing or extra keys are invalid_item. Account names and transfer IDs are nonempty case-sensitive strings. Amounts are JSON integers, never booleans, in [0,9223372036854775807]; transfer amount is positive. Validate request shape and field types before idempotency checks. deposit {op:'deposit',account,amount} creates or increments an account (zero is allowed); success is {ok:true,account,balance}. Signed 64-bit overflow returns {ok:false,error:'invalid_item'} without mutation. transfer {op:'transfer',transfer_id,from,to,amount} requires two existing distinct accounts; otherwise return {ok:false,error:'invalid_item'}. Insufficient sender balance returns {ok:false,error:'insufficient_funds'}. Success atomically debits and credits and returns {ok:true,transfer_id,from,to,amount,from_balance,to_balance}. Destination overflow returns invalid_item without mutation. transfer_id is globally unique: after shape/type validation, an exact replay of an identical successful transfer returns the original response without applying again, even if current balances have changed; any differing field under that ID returns {ok:false,error:'idempotency_conflict'} before account/balance state checks. Failed transfers do not consume IDs. list {op:'list'} returns {ok:true,accounts:[{account,balance}]} including zero balances, sorted by SQLite binary lexical order. Any valid JSON non-object input, invalid field/value, or unknown operation returns exactly {ok:false,error:'invalid_item'}. All failures preserve state.
